Anna Chen: Heads-up — FinRegCo is pushing for per-tenant egress IP guarantees + on-prem peering options. They want a PRD + acceptance criteria by EOD Friday. Can we scope?
Raj Patel: Did they say BGP or they want NAT static IP?
Anna Chen: Both. Primary via customer-managed BGP; fallback NAT from our edge if BGP session fails. They need deterministic source IPs for allowlists.
Emily Torres: Important: we should list failure modes. BGP flap -> immediate failover, ensure session downtime < 30s for SLA. Also asymmetric routing checks.
Marco Diaz: Agree. Also need to clarify L4 vs L7 load balancing on their side. If they terminate TLS, our cert expectations change.
Leah Kim: Draft acceptance criteria idea: 1) Per-tenant static IPv4 egress (x.x.x.x) 2) BGP session established and validated in 60s 3) Failover path provides same logical IP or documented fallback mapping 4) Test harness to replay 1M tokens/hour with preserved source IPs.
Raj Patel: Add: telemetry hooks for BGP state, route advertisement validation, and automatic alerting (pager) on route withdraw.
Anna Chen: I'll start a short PRD. Quick question: do we support advertising customer prefixes (they own ASN) or do we NAT to our IPs? FinRegCo will want their own ASN later.
Marco Diaz: Two phased approach: Phase 1 (MVP) = customer-managed egress by NAT with static mapping + controlplane handshake. Phase 2 = advertise customer prefix / BGP mesh (requires compliance + routing ops signoff).
Emily Torres: Phase 1 acceptance tests: deploy a private tenant, configure egress mapping via this sample config: 
```
tenant: finregco
egress_policy:
  mode: nat
  nat_ip: 203.0.113.45
  health_check: /health/egress
  alert_on_withdraw: true
```
Run replay tool against customer endpoint, confirm source IP seen as 203.0.113.45.
Leah Kim: Phase 2 acceptance tests: BGP session established using CSR + peering key, verify prefix counts and prep for RPKI? also document 'no-export' expectations.
Anna Chen: Should we require customer-provided LR test window? They need to sign an egress RFC acceptance checklist.
Raj Patel: Yes — include handoff template with required fields: ASN, prefixes, contact oncall, allowed ports/ips, MTU, BFD preferences.
Marco Diaz: Edge-case: mixed IPv6 customers — do we NAT64? We should explicitly say IPv6 egress is out-of-scope for MVP.
Emily Torres: Also call out edge-case: overlapping CIDRs between customer and our internal overlay — must error out during validation.
Anna Chen: Ops-bot: create ticket template for eng-oncall and netops when a customer requests private egress.
ops-bot: Created NET-1427 and assigned to @Marco Diaz. ETA for initial validation: 2 business days. :white_check_mark:
Leah Kim: UX/Config idea: a one-page egress summary that includes failover mapping and test URL for customer to validate. Useful for sales handoff.
Raj Patel: For rollout criteria: (a) internal deployment to staging with 3 tenants, (b) soak for 72h with simulated route flaps, (c) run security review for customer-managed BGP.
Marco Diaz: Security note: when advertising customer prefixes we must ensure route filtering to prevent hijack. Add an automated RPKI check and validation runbook.
Anna Chen: OK — next steps: I'll push a short PRD with Phases 1/2, explicit acceptance criteria, test plan, and handoff checklist. @Raj @Marco please review for networking specifics; @Emily @Leah please review test & UX bits. I'll ping again once draft is up.
Emily Torres: I can take test harness ownership. Will sketch replay steps and automation.
Raj Patel: I'll review BGP requirements.
Marco Diaz: On it.
Leah Kim: I'll prototype the egress summary page.
Anna Chen: Thanks team. Quick timer: aim to have PRD ready for eng-platform weekly review on Wednesday.
Raj Patel: noted. :thumbsup:
Anna Chen: End.
